interest: Reveals wartime intelligence cooperation with Mexico, debunking espionage rumors, and legal complexities in repatriating interned Japanese nationals.
overview: This file contains U.S. State Department, FBI, FCC, and diplomatic records from 1942 to 1949 documenting investigations into suspected Japanese espionage, propaganda, and subversive activities in Mexico. Key subjects include the surveillance of the Academia de la Lengua Japonesa in Tacubaya, the debunking of press reports regarding a clandestine radio transmitter in Los Mochis, statements concerning Axis intelligence contacts, allegations against the Unión Nacional Sinarquista, and post-war legal deliberations regarding the deportation and transit of interned Japanese national Masao Imuro Ota.
